newsitem.title: USA: Clinton hails Senate rejection of budget amendment.
newsitem.headline: Clinton hails Senate rejection of budget amendment.

text.p: President Clinton on Tuesday applauded the Senate's rejection of a constititional amendment to require a balanced budget, saying the proposal would have had a ruinous impact on U.S. economic policy.
He also urged legislators to take statutory action that would bring the federal budget into balance by 2002.

"I am pleased that the Senate has heeded the warning of eminent economists and constitutional experts from across the political spectrum and defeated the balanced budget constitutional amendment," Clinton said in a statement issued while he was surveying tornado damage in his home state.

Clinton said the proposed amendment "could have caused or worsened recessions, permitted a minority of legislators to hold the nation's creditworthiness hostage, involved unelected judges in spending and tax policy and threatened social security and other vital benefits."
"While I oppose a constitutional amendment, I am committed to achieving the bipartisan goal of balancing the budget by 2002," he said.

"Now that the amendment vote has taken place, I call on Congress to join me in passing a plan to balance the budget by 2002 while protecting our values, strengthening education and providing targeted tax relief to working families," Clinton said.
"It's time to do the real work of balancing the budget," he said.
